newsitem.title: GERMANY: German IFW institute sees 15 bln DM tax shortfall.
newsitem.headline: German IFW institute sees 15 bln DM tax shortfall.

text.p: Germany's IfW economic institute said on Wednesday it expected official tax estimates due in May to expose a shortfall in total government tax revenues of 15 billion marks this year.
But economist Alfred Boss told Reuters the IfW was reducing its forecast for the budget deficit to 3.3 percent of GDP from an earlier view of 3.5 percent.
That deficit forecast exceeds the three percent which the Maastricht treaty requires countries to hit this year if they are to be judged eligible to join European monetary union in 1999.

Germany has insisted on a strict interpretation of the treaty, but Boss said he was sure that European leaders would use the leeway written into its text allowing states to miss the target as long as they were moving in the right direction.
"European monetary union will definitely not fail over the German deficit," Boss told Reuters.
Boss said that the IfW had revised its deficit forecast because of changes made by Germany's Federal Statistics Office to final figures for 1996.
